d5_arrive: Day five. The tamperers. Yesterday, at many wants at once, you watched competing feelings and thoughts temper your desire — and asked for longer there. Today that station is the anchor, and the tamperers are the material. One more change: the guidance is sparse now. Stations are named, not instructed — you carry the instructions, after four days. If one doesn't come back, ask for it — the button is beside the dwell, and asking is data, not failure. Timers start at zero, as always. Begin when you're ready.
d5_soak1: First voice. Hudson, on the lens itself. Don't-wanting isn't a want. I don't want that — is a way to not actually feel the feeling of wanting. — And: the trying to make the wanting go away, either through aversion or through craving, is the thing that causes the suffering. Rather than: oh, cool — there's wanting.
d5_soak1_verify: So a don't-want isn't the opposite of a want. It's an exit from feeling one. Playing not to lose.
d5_soak2: Second voice. Hudson, on what the tamperers say. The three stories that people tell themselves: people will let me down. People will get angry at me. Or — I'm going to look selfish. Maybe also: I'm bad for having a want. — And the war those stories run: I'm not allowed to want this thing. But I want it. But I'm not allowed to want it. But I want it. There's a lot of war that comes with that.
d5_soak2_verify: Every tamperer runs one of those stories. And every story guards something — a want that never got to be felt directly. That's the day's claim, and the sit will test it.
d5_soak3: The last voice is yours, from yesterday. It was interesting to watch competing feelings, and competing thoughts, that were trying to temper my desire. I think it'd be useful to spend a little bit longer here. — Today is that longer. Before the sit, one move from Hudson: the advance list. Which tamperers can you already see coming? Name them now, out loud — the shoulds, the fears, the prioritizing voices. He calls this playing to win, rather than playing not to lose.
d5_practice_intro: The sit. The sweep runs settle to whole body, then the anchor. Today the narration only names each station — you supply the instruction, from four days of practice. If a station doesn't come back, tap the instruction, beside the dwell, and it plays. Asking is data, not failure: every ask tells tomorrow what to review. And notice which handle arrives when you reach — her quality, or his verb. Whichever comes is your answer to yesterday's question. The chime is permission, not a demand.
d5_prompt_sweep: The sweep, from recall. Anything to note, before the anchor? Tap, and speak. Or continue.
d5_anchor: Many wants at once. The anchor — today it runs long. Let the wants of this actual day arise together: what you want from the rest of it, felt in the body, before any plan. All of them at once, moving freely, none suppressed. — And now the day's work. You know what comes: feelings and thoughts that move against the desire. Tampering. Today they're not interruptions — they're the material. When a tamperer arrives — a should, a fear, a prioritizing voice, an I'm-not-allowed — don't push it away, and don't obey it. Catch it. Feel where it lives in the body. It will present as not-a-want: a rule, a worry, a reasonable objection. The claim to test: that's armor. Inside it, a want is being protected. People will let me down — the want to be met. People will get angry — the want to be safe, to stay connected. I'll look selfish — the want to be good, to be seen as good. Find the want inside the armor, and let it join the others. All of them in the same space, on the same ground — the wants, and the wants inside the tamperers. Nothing to choose. Nothing to solve. This is the inventory, taken by feel. Stay as long as you want.
d5_prompt_inventory: The inventory. Name what you caught — each tamperer, and the want you found inside it. If one wouldn't open, name that too. Tap, and speak.
d5_sayitback: Say it back. What is a don't-want? In your own words: what did the tamperers turn out to be — and what do you do with one, when you catch it? Tap, and speak, when ready.
d5_sayitback_sources: The course's answer, to check against — not to grade. Hudson: don't-wanting isn't a want. It's a way to not feel the feeling of wanting — an exit. The tamperer presents as a rule, a fear, a reasonable objection. Treated as armor, it opens: inside is a want that never got to be felt — to be met, to be safe, to be good. Catching one means: feel the tamper itself, find the want inside it, let that want join the others. Playing to win, rather than playing not to lose. Whatever you found is data for the build.
d5_close: That's the day. In the field: when a want gets tempered today — a should, a flinch, an I-need-to-prioritize — give it the same ten seconds. Feel the temper itself. Find the want inside it. Then choose, if choosing is needed. Export when you're ready. Day six comes from what you found.
